title: [finding] Six `retiredKey()` tombstones tell authors a key "was removed in @objectstack/spec 18" — a version that does not exist; the package is 17.4.0 and every retirement now ships `minor`
body:
⚠️ **Re-filed** — original destroyed with the `os-musk` suspension. Re-measured today on `origin/main`. Bare and **ungraded**.

Six `retiredKey()` tombstone prescriptions under `packages/spec/src` name `@objectstack/spec` **18**:

```
packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-lifecycle-advanced.zod.ts:79   PluginHealthCheck.autoRestart
packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-lifecycle-advanced.zod.ts:85   PluginHealthCheck.maxRestartAttempts
packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-lifecycle-advanced.zod.ts:93   PluginHealthCheck.restartBackoff
packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-lifecycle-advanced.zod.ts:291  …'distributed'
packages/spec/src/kernel/plugin-lifecycle-advanced.zod.ts:320  HotReloadConfig.watchPatterns
packages/spec/src/system/cache.zod.ts:177                      CacheWarmup.strategy: 'scheduled'
```

`@objectstack/spec` is at **17.4.0** ⇒ every one tells an author the key left in a release that does not exist.

**Lit control:** `removed in @objectstack/spec 17` resolves across many files (`ai/agent.zod.ts`, `ai/skill.zod.ts`, `ai/tool.zod.ts`, …) ⇒ the grep finds tombstones of the other spelling, so these six are a real reading.

## Why the number is wrong

The string names the **npm package**; `packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts` defines that field as "the version that removed it". The three siblings that say `17` were removed in **17.0.0**, where npm major and protocol major coincided. The two numbers only decouple on the **launch-window `minor` route** — which is the route all six take. Siblings on that route spell the npm release: `view.pageName` → `17.5.0`, `SessionUser.language` → `17.4.0`, `themes` → `17.1`.

⭐ **Now settled by maintainer ruling** (2026-09-13, 「A,统一 minor,把规则写进 ADR-0087」): every retirement ships `minor` ⇒ the shipping release is `17.x.y` ⇒ **all six are wrong**, not just the one that surfaced this. ADR-0087 now carries the rule, including that a tombstone names the npm release it ships in.

⚠️ Reportedly **four of the six are already published** in `17.4.0`'s `dist/`. ⛔ This seat did not verify the published tarball — re-check the published/unreleased split before acting. The on-tree count above is this seat's own reading.

## No gate sees it

`check:spec-changes`, `check:upgrade-guide` and `check:generated` all read **exit 0** with the wrong number in place ⇒ the silent-shipping class: a prescription printed **at an author**, wrong, with nothing mechanical to catch it.

⛔ Not a find-and-replace: the right number per tombstone is the release that actually shipped each removal, and those differ. Re-derive each.
